metadata.title: Insurance for people and livelihoods: micro and meso
metadata.disclaimer: Listing is not endorsement and is not financial, insurance or investment advice.
metadata.scope: Structured evidence map, not an exhaustive census. Product-years, distribution channels, frameworks and commercial offerings are explicitly separated.
metadata.method: Targeted worldwide web searches prioritised South/Southeast Asia, then other hot lower-/middle-income settings. Primary product, institutional, regulatory and study documents were opened; news used where primary named-scheme details were not found. Checked means retrieved on the date, not independently audited.

evidence_labels.concept: Designed, not yet tried by the people it is for
evidence_labels.reported: Operator or news account, not independent evaluation
evidence_labels.evaluated: External evaluation; commissioning, design and causal limits separately stated

metadata.source_kind_vs_evidence_label: Source titles/genres are separate from the six evidence-status labels. Enrolment figures are operator claims unless explicitly independently measured.
metadata.money_rules: Numeric amounts are in a separate ledger and copied into relevant scheme fields. No totals across years, stages, populations or perils. Member contribution, premium, insured limit and actual payout are distinct. USD conversions are reporting equivalents, not transaction rates.
metadata.trigger_rules: Payout, clinical eligibility, warning, preventive action and donor-cash thresholds are distinct. Missing calculation/verification agents are not guessed.
metadata.status_rules: Ended can mean the specified policy period ended; it does not establish programme closure. Active commercial offering means marketed, not verified sales. Unclear is not never-triggered.
metadata.geographic_limit: No additional qualifying issued micro/meso heat contract was verified in Latin America or Africa in this search. This is a search finding, not proof none exist.

evidence_of_effect.intervention: SEWA / HERA HERInsura insurance and cash-assistance bundle
evidence_of_effect.place: Ten districts in Gujarat and Rajasthan, India
evidence_of_effect.design: External university-authored, HERA-commissioned, non-randomised post-only comparison; SEWA field interviews.
evidence_of_effect.sample: Headline sample 1,022 women: 584 intervention and 438 comparison. Item denominators vary; one descriptive table totals differently.
evidence_of_effect.outcome: Self-reported household coping, health and confidence
evidence_of_effect.result: Programme participants reported better outcomes on some measures. Self-rated health means were 3.44 versus 2.91 on a five-point scale (table headers n=577 and 434). This is an association, not a causal insurance effect.
evidence_of_effect.limits: No random allocation or individual baseline; geographic, occupational and other differences; self-report; commissioned evaluation; insurance cannot be separated from cash assistance. Inconsistent table denominators require clarification.

source.label: George Washington University-authored / HERA-commissioned evaluation (2026), 2025 HERInsura

evidence_of_effect.design: Participant survey and focus groups; comparisons by location/training, without an untreated baseline.
evidence_of_effect.sample: 410 survey respondents: 196 Ahmedabad, 109 Vadodara, 105 Surat; 18 focus groups. Intensive-training subgroup is not a randomised treatment.
evidence_of_effect.outcome: Understanding, experience of insurance and reported coping/use
evidence_of_effect.result: Study documents awareness and payment experiences, with identification/bank matching and understanding of ERA5 versus local weather as practical issues.
evidence_of_effect.limits: No causal estimate of health, income, debt or work-rest effects. Paid subgroup differs from whole survey. Results cannot be extrapolated to all low-income workers.
